goal: Todd runs his software factory from one dashboard with two jobs: running the factory (inner loop) and improving it between builds (outer loop). Traces: R1a; PL (25 Oct, "Two jobs"); I 39-40.

items.want: I want the board to open first, with Decision support one tap away
items.so: what needs me now is what I see first, and history is close when I want it
ac: Opening the dashboard shows the board.
A "Decision support" link on the board opens Decision support in one tap.
Every other screen has a way back to the board.

items.want: I want the board to show only the cards the machine is building or has built
items.so: all card work goes through one place I can watch
ac: Every card on the board is one the machine worked on, whatever models and providers it used.
Cards worked by hand appear only in Linear.
notes: Agents opened by hand were used only because Start didn't exist yet.

items.want: I want one tile per card, with the agents working on it inside
items.so: one card never shows up as several
ac: A running card with three agents shows as one tile listing three agents.

items.want: I want the board's stages to be Linear's statuses
items.so: the board and Linear always agree
ac: The stages are Backlog, Ready, Implementation, Evidence review, Remediation, Staging/smoke test, UAT, Complete, in that order.
Moving a card in Linear moves it on the board.
notes: Code review, Triage, Canceled and Duplicate are left off.

items.want: on my phone, I want stages that fold to one line
items.so: 30 Backlog cards never bury the live work
ac: A folded stage shows its name and card count on one line.
On load, only stages holding a running, stuck or waiting card are open.
Tapping a stage opens or folds it.
notes: Todd's own layout. Rejected: columns scrolling sideways; one column at a time by tabs.

items.want: I want each card to show only its title and status until I tap it
items.so: I can scan a stage quickly and open only what I care about
ac: Each card in an open stage shows its title and a status pill.
Tapping a card expands it in place; tapping again collapses it.

items.want: I want finished cards to stay on the board until their project is done
items.so: finished work clears in batches, not one by one
ac: A Complete card stays while its Linear project is open.
When the project is marked Completed, its cards leave the board.
notes: Every piece of work gets its own Linear project, the dashboard included.

items.want: I want to see at a glance when a running card is stuck

ac: A card waiting on me shows an amber "Waiting on you" pill with its own icon.

items.want: I want a running card to say what it is doing now and when it last did something

rules.text: Every screen works on phone and desktop equally, reached through Tailscale.
Todd is the only user; there is no sign-in beyond Tailscale.

Glance, don't read: status as pictures and charts, the most important thing where the eye lands first, plain words with no agent jargon, only what Todd needs with detail one tap away, each view fitting a phone screen.
The Mint & Iris look of picture 12 (light, mint, iris, amber for waiting on you, rose for stuck, Public Sans). Status is never shown by colour alone.
Labels and values are never cut off.
Rose means a problem or a destructive action (Stuck, Stopped, Stop, Didn't start); other button colours carry no meaning (decisions 0019, 0029).
Every screen has an empty, a loading and a failed state; a failed screen never looks like an empty one (decision 0035).
A picture counts only for what it was drawn to show; the frame Stitch drew around it is not built.
On desktop, the board follows picture 01's look and column layout; every other screen is the phone layout, widened.
Each screen is proven by Todd seeing it work on that screen.
Several cards can run at once; the board shows all of them.
Decision support covers all cards, with no date or project filter.
Out of scope: editing a card's text (stays in Linear); showing raw traces on screen (only the link); the old dashboard, its mockup and Julia's DESIGN.md as a starting point.

build.text: The part that starts, watches and stops builds (nothing exists on main since 26 Oct). The runner is a Mastra workflow (Todd, 27 Oct).
Save the choices made at every Start, so the next Start can reuse them.
Record each request with its pstack role (today only the stock agent type and model are recorded).
Record each stop's cause and root-cause stage as data (today only time and question).
Record verdicts and send-backs as data, not only as prose in Linear.
Record when a card's retro is complete, then delete its trace.
The runner (a Mastra workflow) that starts and watches builds also monitors each agent and records its context fill and compactions, where the dashboard can read them (Todd, 27 Oct).
Route Todd's answer to the running build.
Prove effort reaches every helper (Mastra Code sets it per session).
Keep the model list from Todd's three accounts, priced from the current price (free only while it actually costs nothing), refreshing itself; look up missing prices.
Run pstack's Shipping around UAT: the checker reports each "done means" line, then preview and smoke test, then UAT, then Shipping lands it after Todd's yes.
The automatic smoke test against the preview (deferred in main's plan; goes through the front door as its own work).
Per-card limit: a setting for its value, a check while a card runs, and the notification and Needs you item when the card passes it.
Whatever creates a wait on Todd adds a row; its kind decides the buttons, where each goes, when the row leaves and whether it pulses.
Create the Linear label "Needs settled" and have the planner agent apply it when it finishes shaping a card.
The runner marks a piece of a card as waiting for Todd's yes, with screenshots and video, while the card stays in its stage.

comments.text: Each picture counts only for what it was drawn to show; the frame Stitch drew (header, bell, profile icon, bottom menu, "Live sync", a second Needs-you bar) is not built.
The desktop board follows picture 01 for its look and column layout only; the other screens are the phone layout widened, judged on content and look.
Spec lines built without a picture are judged on content and plain words, so a first version may look plainer than the drawn parts.
"PULSE" on the expanded running card is jargon; use plain words.
The "Step 4 of 8" bar on picture 03 is replaced by the checklist on picture 04.
"Linear notification sent" is not repeated on each Needs-you row; every item sends one.
The Needs-you title reads "Needs you (6)", with the count.
On the Start screen, Main session appears only at the top, not inside a group.
Role explanations show only when the ⓘ is tapped, as a small popup.
No cost estimates, no "Capped at", no Slack, and pstack's real role names only (all were Stitch inventions).
Judgment's "$$$$" for GPT-6 Sol is a drawing error; prices come from the real model list.
The design-system card (picture 12) is the colour reference; a later copy in Stitch drifted darker.
On the Decision support map, the stray "RK" and the overlapping Sol and Opus bubbles are drawing flaws.
Ranked and Cards were drawn before the switch existed: both sit behind the Map / Ranked / Cards switch, without their top banners.
The one-line notes on each finished card (Cards view) are Stitch's invention.
"Todd's Recommendation" is renamed "Suggestion": it is the dashboard's idea, not Todd's.
